None of the four solutions gives the constant I expect, so I reject all of them.

**Solution 1 (18/7):** The reducibility claims are asserted rather than proved, and the discharging only checks charges once those claims are granted. My recollection of the literature on proper conflict-free list coloring of sparse graphs points to 16/7, not 18/7. I can't verify that recollection without tools, so this rejection is provisional.

**Solution 2 (2/3):** This answers a different question. It treats weak Sidon sets and 3-term arithmetic progressions, which has nothing to do with conflict-free list coloring or maximum average degree. The claimed construction and the transversal bound are also unsupported. Rejected as off-target.

**Solution 3 (36/11):** The proof is incomplete. Its own discharging gives degree-3 vertices a final charge of 3, below the claimed 36/11, and it then waves this away with "a refined analysis" that is never carried out. The tightness example is also not verified. Rejected.

**Solution 4 (18/5):** The charge bookkeeping is stated loosely. The 3-vertex and $k$-vertex cases are asserted with no concrete rule. The value 18/5 is well above the threshold I expect, so the claimed sufficiency would be false. Rejected.

Since none of the four gives the constant I expect (16/7, from memory and not checked), the correct choice is NONE.

CHOICE: NONE
